verdict: axiom_conditional_stability is the stronger general-principle prototype, but neither candidate is established or judge-qualified

dimensions.fundamentality: Conditional retention/error-modulated decay applies to arbitrary channels and could couple memory with adaptation, though this implementation only predicts and does not derive action or other abilities. agency_options aims at a general action principle but currently computes one-step free-cell area on a fixed 10x10 Snake board.
dimensions.novelty: No literature results were returned by shared/lit.py searches, so no source-verified novelty claim is possible. Conditional prediction plus error-modulated forgetting and reachable-space/empowerment-style action selection both have obvious prior-art neighborhoods; the code does not establish a new law.
dimensions.scaling: axiom_conditional_stability stores and scans dense O(n^2) source-target-bit tables per step, limiting large-n prospects unless sparsity emerges from the principle. agency_options is cheap on its fixed board but hard-codes board dimensions and observation layout, so its current scaling is not domain-general.

axiom_conditional_stability.mechanism: Per-source/target Bernoulli counts with fixed pseudocounts and target-surprise-modulated decay.

agency_options.mechanism: One-step flood-fill area minus hard-coded Manhattan distance to apple; fixed Snake 10x10 observation and restart detection.

verdict: axiom_conditional_stability is the stronger current prototype; neither establishes a new fundamental law or passes the judge

dimensions.fundamentality: The axiom states a domain-general coupling between predictive usefulness and persistence, but implementation applies target-wide error decay to every pair and only predicts. Growth couples surprise-triggered edge birth with pruning, a richer growth/removal story, but birth creates every incoming source edge for the surprised target, so sparsity is not derived. Both leave memory, exploration, and action largely unaccounted for.
dimensions.novelty: No exact equivalent was verified. Opened pyhgf paper (arXiv:2410.09206) explicitly discusses surprising inputs and structural adaptation in predictive-coding networks, establishing close prior-art territory for growth nucleation; predictive error-modulated retention also sits within known predictive coding and adaptive-forgetting traditions. Novelty remains unproven, not disproved.
dimensions.scaling: Axiom allocates and scans dense O(n^2) pair tables, with measured memory exponent 2.0. Growth has measured exponent about 2.03 and width-64 edge count 3009->3218 over four phases; creating O(n) incoming links per surprising target drives near-dense structure and weakens its claimed sparse scaling. Neither has evidence for scale robustness.

growth_nucleation.mechanism: All non-self source-target edges are created on target prediction error >0.12; retention uses conditional-rate contrast and fixed decay; pruning requires age > support and utility < prune.

axiom_conditional_stability.mechanism: Dense source-target two-state counts; target prediction error modulates decay with floor; per target choose strongest conditional-rate contrast, counting it active above 0.2.
